input.subject: Jinbe
input.continuity: One Piece manga through the end of Wano Country arc
input.intent: Perform a PRICE-ONLY balance refinement of this newly generated same-campaign Jinbe using the standard pipeline. Halve base cost850 to425 and halve each of15 purchase costs exactly. Exact path costs in order: Bodily-Water Force [130,210,525,1050,2300]; Moisture-Carried Shock [110,240,550,1150,2400]; Observation and Contact Discipline [140,190,475,950,2050]. Preserve EVERY other field EXACTLY, including all complete approved descriptions, names, IDs, form, attacks, Technique unlocks, controls, resources and modifiers. Do not shorten or paraphrase descriptions to save output space: their source/lifecycle boundaries were independently reviewed. Return the entire valid unit, not a patch. These costs are provisional numerical game tuning from bounded encounter evidence, not canon measurements. No new water power, defensive ability or alteration to the shared Karate armor-pressure adaptation is requested.

candidateToRefine.name: Jinbe — Knight of the Sea
candidateToRefine.description: Straw Hat helmsman, adapted from the One Piece manga through Wano's departure, excluding Chapter 1058 and later material. A stocky blue whale-shark fish-man with webbed hands, gills, lower fangs, left-eye scar, gold-striped black hair and topknot, Sun Pirates chest tattoo, diamond-patterned kimono and wave-patterned coat. Stationary unarmed combat uses Fish-Man Karate, bounded Jujutsu displacement, Armament armor pressure and Observation-based acquisition. No Devil Fruit or transformation. Samegawara Seiken is the primary bodily-water force punch; internal damage purchases approximate its defense penetration, not advanced Armament or universal defense negation. Karate remains usable on dry land. All numbers, prices, resource costs, tier schedules and repeated attacks are provisional game tuning, not canon measurements or measured balance. The single Technique changes with highest purchased tier, not path identity. Water-supply gating is absent: Uchimizu, Yarinami, Murasame, Mizugokoro, both liquid Kairyu throws and Raizo-water distribution are omitted. Buraikan implements only its piercing shock and knockback, omitting its gathered-water presentation rather than generating water. Kairagi and Samehada Shotei are defensive blocks and are omitted, as are defensive durability, rescue movement, underwater enhancement, swimming, fish communication and transport, negotiation, blood transfusion and weapon history. Helmsmanship grants no ally range. No shields, taunt, tower HP, Supreme King Haki, future sight, terrain creation or arbitrary teleportation. Enemy motion and control response belong to the encounter caller.

techniques.name: Fish-Man Karate Ogi: Buraikan — Vagabond Drill

paths.name: Bodily-Water Force
paths.description: Armor-pressure specialization for Samegawara Seiken and every contextual Technique. Internal fraction is a bounded Karate abstraction, including its application to the crushing grip and throw; it is not proof that every named move has identical water mechanics. Flat additions precede multipliers, then internal splitting; remaining armor affects only ordinary damage. Neither internal damage nor armor ignore defeats invulnerability. Highest tier 1 unlocks full stamina and Soshark on every path. Soshark's brief slow approximates a crushing hold, not broken-limb simulation; it requires slowable. At tier 2, Uzushio replaces Soshark rather than adding another button. Its displacement moves an eligible displaceable target back by at most 6 path units, clamped at the entrance, not to a chosen coordinate. Hikishio's defensive counter sequence is omitted. Shared 14–18 reach bounds are an authored contact envelope for grips and throws, not stretched arms.

upgrades.name: Samegawara Seiken — Transmitted Force
upgrades.description: Sets internal fraction to 0.15 for primary attacks and all Techniques. Also reaches the global tier-1 Soshark and stamina unlock.

upgrades.name: Armament — Hardened Hands
upgrades.description: Ignores 20% of armor reduction on ordinary damage. Helps the primary and all Techniques against armor; it does not remove armor or grant defensive hardening.

upgrades.name: Samegawara Seiken — Deeper Transmission
upgrades.description: Raises internal fraction from 0.15 to 0.35. This is a stronger bounded armor bypass, not unrestricted Devil Fruit negation.

upgrades.name: Onigawara Seiken — Armament Force
upgrades.description: Multiplies primary and Technique damage by 1.35 and raises armor ignore to 0.4. Abstracts the force and hardening of Demon Brick Fist into existing attacks; its separate noncontact finishing animation and black lightning are omitted, not treated as Supreme King Haki.

upgrades.name: Secret-Art Penetration
upgrades.description: Raises internal fraction to 0.6 and adds 20 damage to the primary and all Techniques before multiplication. Highest tier 5 also replaces the contextual button with Buraikan.

paths.name: Moisture-Carried Shock
paths.description: Line-collateral specialization. Emission is a bounded continuation of Karate force beyond contact, not thrown water or an additional primary attack. Only this path owns emission. Later configurations replace earlier ones; successful positive-damage primary cycles count once, irrespective of collateral. Techniques never count. Emissions exclude flat additions, stop at obstacles and cannot trigger further effects. At highest tier 3, Karakusagawara replaces Uzushio; tier 4 retains it. This atmospheric-moisture wave uses aimed projectile flight to preserve delayed arrival, not homing. It launches toward the selected coordinate after windup and arrives after distance/24 seconds. Moving more than 5 units from that coordinate causes a complete miss with no collateral. Its area cap includes the primary target; collateral may exceed acquisition reach but must satisfy impact visibility and obstruction checks. Its 4-unit displacement requires displaceable. This compact impact disk bounds the source's broader shockwave rather than simulating an expanding front.

upgrades.name: Contact Envelope
upgrades.description: Adds 2 reach to primary acquisition and its contextual Techniques. This is placement tolerance for close combat, not swimming or free movement.

upgrades.name: Shock Continuation
upgrades.description: Every fourth successful primary cycle emits 16 damage along a 4-wide, 14-long continuation from contact away from Jinbe, capped at 3 targets.

upgrades.name: Wider Follow-Through
upgrades.description: Replaces emission with 24 damage, width 7, length 20 and cap 5, still every fourth successful primary cycle. Highest tier 3 also unlocks the delayed Karakusagawara Technique.

upgrades.name: Sustained Shock Rhythm
upgrades.description: Replaces emission with 30 damage every third successful primary cycle, width 8, length 24 and cap 6. Lowering the threshold makes continuation more frequent.

upgrades.name: Piercing Follow-Through
upgrades.description: Replaces emission with 44 damage every second successful primary cycle, width 10, length 30 and cap 8. This primary collateral remains distinct from the tier-5 single-target Buraikan Technique.

paths.name: Observation and Contact Discipline
paths.description: Reliable acquisition and primary-cycle throughput, not future sight or enemy-motion simulation. Detection handles concealment only; obstacles and invulnerability remain separate checks. Retargeting can replace one lost primary target at resolution without restarting windup, never a Technique target. At highest tier 5 on any path, Buraikan replaces Karakusagawara: concentrated damage and up to 10 units of eligible backward displacement replace the broad delayed area wave. This does not assert a canonical strength ranking. Technique requests record target, base form and selected Technique; they queue for the next primary cycle. Commit rechecks eligibility, selection, funding and the shared cooldown, then spends 40 stamina and starts 10 seconds of cooldown. Cancellation before commit spends nothing and resumes primary acquisition. Each Technique replaces one primary cycle with its own windup and recovery; timing purchases affect only primaries. Stamina recovers at 5 per encounter second in this sole, non-draining base form. Purchases never refill it; reset restores full stamina and clears attacks, counters and cooldowns.

upgrades.name: Observation — Sense Presence
upgrades.description: Enables concealed-target detection for primary attacks and Techniques. A bounded adaptation of presence sensing, not sight through obstacles.

upgrades.name: Veteran Target Correction
upgrades.description: Enables one primary retarget at resolution when its original target is lost. Does not rescue a locked Technique or bypass reach and obstruction.

upgrades.name: Compact Karate Rhythm
upgrades.description: Multiplies primary windup and period by 0.85. More frequent successful primaries also build purchased emission counters faster; Technique timing is unchanged.

upgrades.name: Gosenmaigawara Seiken — Committed Punch
upgrades.description: Adds 12 damage to the primary and all Techniques. Abstracts the powerful 5,000 Brick Fist into outgoing strike force; the tile count is not a damage multiplier.

upgrades.name: Master's Contact Rhythm
upgrades.description: Further multiplies primary timing by 0.8, for a cumulative factor of 0.68 on this path, and adds 2 reach. Improves acquisition opportunity without moving Jinbe, guaranteeing hits or accelerating Techniques.

context.independentReview: Measured5000-credit results: old Jinbe armored boss424 below Zoro623 and repriced Luffy574. Actual displacement72 path units at2650 spend vs Luffy144 at2900. Halving Jinbe prices projects boss916 at5000 while dense2348/concealed2168 remain below crowd specialists.0.75x failed to open a specialist armor niche. At1000 projected dense688/boss226: strong armor efficiency without crowd dominance. All64 legal build/form policies included; no new damage measurements claimed by price projection.

knowledge.subject: Jinbe
gaps: All five supplied captures were read through their ends, including later technique sections, references and navigation. Each reports acquisitionTruncated=false. Linked manga chapters, images and external pages were not independently inspected; citations identify only the supplied sources.

The requested continuity is supported, but the wiki pages are not snapshots restricted to Wano. The cutoff is treated as the Wano conclusion and departure, not subsequent revelations. The 1,100,000,000 bounty and associated senior-officer presentation cite Chapter 1058, explicitly described by the source as post-Wano, and are not adopted as cutoff facts.

Excluded post-Wano techniques: Gosenmaigawara Shuto / Five Thousand Brick Chop (Chapter 1111), Kata Guruma / Piggyback (Chapter 1117), and Umigumo Ipponzeoi / Sea Cloud Shoulder Throw (Chapter 1145). Their presence in later sections was checked, not overlooked.
The marine-life ability is supported before Wano, but its name Shark Network / Same Joho mo is sourced to Chapter 1130 and is not adopted as an in-scope named technique.

Excluded later material includes Egghead and Elbaph outfits, Bonney-induced childhood reversion, S-Shark's separate abilities, the Mecha-Shark rescue, and Observation Haki examples involving Saturn, Mars and the alleged Chapter 1189 Luffy–Imu battle. The latter allegation is not independently verified and is outside scope regardless.

No named combat transformation for Jinbe within the requested cutoff is established by these pages. Armament hardening is recorded as Haki rather than invented as a transformation. Other characters' hybrid forms, Energy Steroid changes and Devil Fruit powers are not Jinbe's.

Excluded non-manga or game-specific Jinbe techniques include Shizurase, Dai Kairyu Keri, Kairyu Shibuki Hashira, and game-only uses of Senmaigawara Seiken, Yabusame and Jujutsu Murasame / Shark Pack. Jinbe's manga Murasame / Rain Shower is a different technique from Hody's shark-shaped Jujutsu Murasame.

Anime-only presentations were not merged into manga techniques, including Gosenmaigawara Seiken's immediate shockwave and different Jailer Beast target, Yarinami's whirlpool staging, and Mizugokoro's glowing orb.

The main page's Quick Answers inconsistently calls Jinbe the ninth member and gives Whole Cake Island as the joining point. The detailed main text distinguishes ninth recruit/tenth member and formal Wano arrival, corroborated by the supplied Wano summary.

The abilities overview says the Wadatsumi roundhouse broke several fingers, while the specific technique entry says one finger. The discrepancy is preserved rather than resolved without further evidence.

Exact numerical technique multipliers, quantified ranges, resource costs and comprehensive weaknesses are not supplied. The Karate page's speculation based on tile counts is not treated as measurement; bodily-water attacks are not assumed to bypass every possible defense.

The abilities page asserts that Jinbe can secrete water, but provides no specific manga reference for that assertion. The detailed Karate page explicitly attributes secretion examples to Hody. Jinbe's self-generated water supply is therefore not established in this record.

Supreme King Haki, future sight, and advanced Armament emission or internal-destruction classifications are not established for Jinbe by the supplied evidence. Black lightning and the adjective 'advanced' are insufficient to assign those specific abilities.
No unsupported memory or caller-invented concept has been included. Navigation lists were not treated as proof that Jinbe possesses other listed characters' powers.

findings.message: Pulse and emission cycles count successful primary attack cycles required for one trigger, not waves per trigger. A cycle counts once when at least one primary hit applies positive damage, regardless of collateral targets. Pulses apply stun without damage; their event amount counts affected targets. Emissions apply their declared damage. Pulse intervals can further limit trigger frequency.

gaps: This is a bounded review of the supplied passages, not independent verification of linked manga panels or the author's prior approval and balance measurements.

The sources mix continuities and later material. Findings use Jinbe's own manga-era abilities through Wano; later Observation examples, clone abilities, game-only techniques and anime-only presentations are not adopted.

Buraikan's gathered-water presentation, defensive blocks and durability, swimming and underwater enhancement, liquid manipulation, marine-life communication, transport and other listed noncombat roles are deliberately omitted, not executable traits of this candidate.

The source supports the underlying martial arts, perception and exertion, not the exact numerical values or the value of the halved prices. Price-only preservation is a separate contract comparison; notably, the current Moisture-Carried Shock description adds 'or counters' relative to the supplied candidateToRefine, so preservation of every non-price field is not exact.
